title: Lamps at home
hook: Bandi Chhor lamps at your own door
tomorrow: can a game in the backyard be holy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, running a chhabeel: cold water, freely, in the heat, and a dad asking whether 'anyone' includes the people at home. Now it's autumn, and dusk comes early.

There's a particular quiet in a house after an argument. Doors close a little harder. People eat at different times. Texts get answered with one word. At Simran's house it's been like that for a few days, and tonight her dad is out on the front step anyway, setting small clay lamps along the edge of the porch, the way he does every autumn. Who are the lamps for? The oldest answer: for someone coming home.
screen: `THE QUIET AFTER AN ARGUMENT.` → `CLAY LAMPS ALONG THE PORCH.` → `FOR SOMEONE COMING HOME.`

segments.voice: The day is Bandi Chhor Divas. Bandi is a prisoner, chhor is release: the day of the one who freed the prisoners. Sikhs remember that Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, was held in the fort at Gwalior, and when his release came, tradition says, he would not walk out alone. The rajas held with him came out too, holding on to his cloak. When he reached Amritsar, people lit lamps to welcome him home. So the lamps at a Sikh door that night aren't decoration. They're a welcome, the way you'd leave the porch light on for someone driving in late. Guru Nanak has a short line that holds the picture: deevaa balai andheraa jaae. When the lamp is lit, the darkness goes. In the next line he turns it inward, to the mind. A lit lamp doesn't argue with the dark; it just makes the way in easier to find. And the Guru's choice adds one more thing: nobody comes home alone. A lamp at the door says, whoever is still out there, the way back is lit. Even for the person you haven't been talking to.
screen: `BANDI CHHOR: THE PRISONERS FREED.` · `HE WOULD NOT WALK OUT ALONE.` · `AMRITSAR LIGHTS LAMPS.` · `THE LAMP LIT, THE DARK GOES.` · then, large: `LAMPS AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Light a candle or switch on one small lamp, if you can, or find the nearest light in the room. Rest your eyes on it for the sit. Each time your thoughts drift to someone you're at odds with, look back at the light, and let that person stand in it for a moment.
Lamps at home. Small lights set at the door and along the windows on Bandi Chhor Divas: a welcome home, and a way back lit for anyone.
Hold onto this: lamps at the door, lit for whoever is still finding the way in. Tonight, two people on one porch.

howItsDone: On Bandi Chhor Divas, in the Diwali season, Sikhs light lamps and candles at home along doors, walls and windowsills, visit the gurdwara for kirtan and Ardas, and share sweets; the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar is lit up that night.

fork.setup: your roommate is out late after a rough day, and you're the last one up. what would the Bandi Chhor lamps do?
options: leave a light on at the door, so the way in is easy, whatever happened today.
turn everything off; a lamp is for a festival, not an ordinary night.
wait up to say how late it is; the light should come with a lesson.
fork.reveal: a lamp at the door is a welcome, not a speech. Amritsar lit lamps for a Guru who wouldn't come home alone.

original.note: Punjabi: bandi, a prisoner; chhor, release. the one who freed the prisoners.

trapdoor: what you thought: festive autumn decorations.
what it means: a welcome home for a Guru who freed others with him, and a lit way back for anyone.
what a scholar hears: Guru Nanak's deevaa balai andheraa jaae (Ang 791): the lamp lit, the dark gone, then turned inward to the mind.
guess: setting lamps at the door to welcome someone home
lighting candles to remember family who have died
stringing up lights to decorate for autumn

chat.says: still not really talking to dad. he's out lighting the diyas. help him or wait till we fix it?
options: Help him. A lamp at the door is a welcome; lighting it together can start the fixing.
Wait. Lamps are for celebrating, so light them once you've made peace.
Light your own on the other side. Each person's lamp is their own prayer.
chat.meaning: Bandi Chhor lamps welcome someone home, and the Guru wouldn't come home alone. A lit door is a way back, even mid-argument.
